study type: Retrospective cohort study using national register data
outcome: Persistent airflow obstruction (FEV1/FVC z-score below lower limit of normal)
cohort: The study included 44,778 individuals aged 7-49 years with asthma or COPD from the Swedish National Airway Register, linked to their birth data from the Medical Birth Register.
finding: Gestational age was the most significant covariate for persistent airflow obstruction across all ages in patients with asthma or COPD, with GA-adjusted birthweight further improving prediction, especially for middle-aged adults born small for GA.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery did not contribute to the risk of persistent airflow obstruction.
birth_weight: GA-adjusted birthweight was measured, with categories including small for GA and appropriate for GA.
gest_age: Gestational age categories included extremely, very, moderate, and late preterm, as well as term and postterm.
